newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- munis off on their own.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- munis off on their own.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were moving somewhat independently of the fading U.S. Treasury market, losing more ground than government securities at midday.
The muni market was quoted off 1/4 to 3/8 in late trade, said one trader. The government long bond was down 11/32 to yield 7.12 percent.

"I could see off an 1/8" and following the Treasury market, the trader said. "But off 3/8, the muni market is moving partly independently of the Treasury market," he said, offering no ready explanation for why munis are underperforming.
"We've given up most of the gains from Tuesday," he added.

The muni market's softness was in part triggered by one economic report. March industrial output rose 0.9 percent to 84.1 percent, the highest rate in two years. The gain exceeded the 0.6 percent increase forecast in a Reuters consensus survey of economists, who looked for the rate to firm to 83.6 percent.
Meanwhile, in the primary market, a brisk pace of issuance continued, the bulk in the negotiated sector.
Municipal bond sales on Wednesday were expected to total $850 million in 27 sales.
Negotiated offerings totaled $793 million in nine sales. On the competitive side, 18 sales totaling $57 million are on the schedule.

The New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority led the pack with the largest negotiated offering, a $383 million issue priced with a top yield of 5.95 percent in 2027, through a syndicate headed by Bear Stearns & Co.
Oregon's sale of $155 million of certificate of participations were priced with a top yield of 5.95 percent in 2024, according to Bear Stearns.
And Yuma, Ariz., Industrial Development Authority fetched 5.90 pcercent in 2017.
In debt futures in early afternoon activity, June Treasury bonds fell 13 ticks to 107-7/32, while June municipal bonds lost 10 ticks to 112-9/32. This left the MOB spread at 162 ticks.
